title: Hitting-Time Bounds for Asynchronous Q-Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.13901v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study the last iterate of standard asynchronous Q-learning from a single trajectory of a finite Markov decision process. The trajectory follows a fixed behavior policy whose state--action chain is irreducible and may be periodic. For discount factor $\gamma$, write $H=(1-\gamma)^{-1}$, and let $\mu_{\min}$ be the minimum stationary state--action probability and $\mathfrak h_\star$ the largest expected hitting time of the reverse state--action chain. We prove that zero-initialized Q-learning with a constant step size achieves sup-norm error at most $\varepsilon$ with high probability using $\widetilde{O}(H^4/(\mu_{\min}\varepsilon^2)+\mathfrak h_\star)$ transitions, for $0<\varepsilon\le1$. The statistical term retains the quartic effective-horizon dependence of standard Q-learning, while initialization cost is additive in $\mathfrak h_\star$. For aperiodic behavior chains, a comparison with mixing time yields a transient term $\wide

translated_title: 异步Q学习的命中时间界
translated_abstract: 我们研究了从有限马尔可夫决策过程的单条轨迹出发的标准异步Q学习的最后一次迭代。该轨迹遵循一个固定的行为策略，其状态-动作链是不可约的，且可能是周期的。对于折扣因子 $\gamma$，记 $H=(1-\gamma)^{-1}$，设 $\mu_{\min}$ 为最小的平稳状态-动作概率，$\mathfrak h_\star$ 为反向状态-动作链的最大期望命中时间。我们证明，对于 $0<\varepsilon\le1$，采用常数步长、零初始化的Q学习能够以高概率在 $\widetilde{O}(H^4/(\mu_{\min}\varepsilon^2)+\mathfrak h_\star)$ 次转移内实现上确界范数误差至多 $\varepsilon$。统计项保留了标准Q学习对有效视野的四次方依赖，而初始化成本以 $\mathfrak h_\star$ 的加性形式出现。对于非周期行为链，通过与混合时间的比较，可得到一个瞬态项 $\widehat{O}$……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文在仅要求状态-动作链不可约（允许周期性）的弱条件下，证明了零初始化、常数步长的异步Q学习只需 $\widetilde{O}(H^4/(\mu_{\min}\varepsilon^2)+\mathfrak h_\star)$ 次转移即可高概率达到 $\varepsilon$ 上确界范数精度，且初始化成本以反向链最大期望命中时间 $\mathfrak h_\star$ 的加性形式出现。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that, under merely irreducible (possibly periodic) behavior chains, zero-initialized asynchronous Q-learning with constant step size achieves $\varepsilon$ sup-norm error with high probability within $\widetilde{O}(H^4/(\mu_{\min}\varepsilon^2)+\mathfrak h_\star)$ transitions, where the initialization cost appears additively as the largest expected hitting time $\mathfrak h_\star$ of the reverse chain.
